# BloomEffect

- Inherits [`PostEffect`](posteffect.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("BloomEffect")`

Controls the glow that bright light spreads onto what is around it. The engine applies bloom without this instance, with the same result as this class's defaults. Adding one overrides the bloom, and one with `Enabled` off turns bloom off, which suits a 2D game whose white sprites should not glow.

When several apply, the first enabled one is used: the children of `Lighting` are considered first, then the camera's.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Intensity` | `number` | `1` | read/write | The strength of the glow, as a multiple of the engine's default. 1 is the default look, 2 is twice the glow, and 0 is none. |
| `Size` | `number` | `24` | read/write | How far the glow spreads, from 0 to 56. 24 is the engine's default. 48 spreads the same light about twice as far, and fainter. |
| `Threshold` | `number` | `1.1` | read/write | How bright a pixel must be, after exposure, before it glows. Exposure brings the average of a frame to about 0.45, so the default blooms pixels a little more than twice as bright as the average. At 0, everything glows a little. |
